author: Rahul kp
title: Mean vs Median
simple_words: Mean shares equally, median is the middle one, mode is the most popular one.

definitions.meaning: Sum of all observations divided by the number of observations. It uses every value in the data.
Median is the middle value of data arranged in order. Mode is the value that occurs most often.

key_points: ==Mean== uses every value, so one very large or small value drags it.
==Median== depends only on position, so extreme values do not disturb it.
==Mode== is the most frequent value; data can have no mode or more than one.
In a symmetrical distribution, mean = median = mode.
formula_hook: pick the average like a pro

formulas.name: Empirical relation
formulas.legend: Holds for a moderately skewed distribution only. Use it to find the third average from two.

rows: Data is even, all values matter
Most common item or size is needed

insight.text: With an extreme value, the mean moves away while median and mode stay put.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Mean Meets all, Median is Middle, Mode is Most
memory_trick.explanation: Mean meets every value in the data. Median stands in the middle of the ordered list. Mode is the most popular value.

steps: Find the middle position or highest frequency
Check for skewness or extreme values
exam_tip: If the question says outliers or open-ended classes, choose median. If it says most common or most frequent, choose mode.

doubt.question: Can mean, median and mode all be different?
doubt.answer: Yes. In a skewed distribution they differ. They are equal only when the distribution is symmetrical.

mistakes.wrong: Taking the middle item without arranging the data in order
mistakes.right: !!Arrange data in ascending or descending order!! first, then locate the middle item.

mistakes.wrong: Saying median is badly affected by extreme values
mistakes.right: Median depends on position, so extreme values do not affect it. The mean is the one affected.

mistakes.wrong: Saying every data set has exactly one mode
mistakes.right: A data set can have no mode, one mode, or several modes.

mistakes.wrong: Using mean as the best average for open-ended classes
mistakes.right: Mean needs class mid-points, which open-ended classes lack. Median is preferred.

check_notes: Checker 1: Table row 1 (Mean, 'Best used when'): 'Data is even' is vague. Better: 'Data is roughly symmetrical with no extreme values, and every value should count.'

Checker 1: Doubt answer: 'They are equal only when the distribution is symmetrical' is too absolute. A symmetrical distribution with two modes has mean = median but a different mode, and the three can be equal by coincidence in data that is not symmetrical. Better: 'In a symmetrical unimodal distribution, mean = median = mode. In a skewed distribution they differ, and in a moderately skewed one the median lies between the mean and the mode.'
Checker 1: Key point 4: add 'unimodal' so it reads: 'In a symmetrical unimodal distribution, mean = median = mode.'

Checker 1: Insight text: 'median and mode stay put' is slightly overstated. If an extreme value is added (rather than replacing a value), the median's position can move by half a place. Better: 'the mean moves a lot, while the median and mode change little or not at all.'
Checker 2: Table row 1, 'Best used when': 'Data is even' is vague. Better: 'Data is fairly symmetrical with no extreme values, and every value matters'.
Checker 2: Insight text: 'median and mode stay put' is slightly loose. Better: 'median and mode are not affected, or only barely affected'.
